title: Steve Reich’s Clapping Music is one 12-beat rhythm clapped against itself
body: On 3 October 2026 the American composer Steve Reich turned 90, and concerts for his birthday, from Soundstreams in Toronto on 6 October to the Barbican in London on 28 October, [programmed](https://www.boosey.com/cr/news/Steve-Reich-at-90-Worldwide-Celebrations-and-Premiere/102858) Clapping Music, his 1972 piece for two people and nothing but their hands. Both clap one rhythm of 12 beats, eight claps and four rests, grouped three, two, one, two. One clapper keeps it the whole way through; the other, every 8 or 12 bars, moves one beat ahead, so the pattern’s first beat goes to the end. Each of the 12 positions lines the claps up differently: one beat ahead, only 4 claps coincide and no beat is silent; at other positions one or two beats fall silent; and after 12 moves the two meet again in unison. Reich has said the idea came after a concert in Brussels in 1972, when his group clapped along with flamenco musicians.

slides.question: In Clapping Music two people clap one rhythm of 8 claps in 12 beats. One moves a beat ahead: how many claps coincide?
slides.explanation: 4 of the 8. The other claps fall alone, and together they fill every one of the 12 beats: no beat is left silent.

slides.alt: Animation on deep plum: a big 90 for Steve Reich, then Clapping Music as two rows of 12 cells, pink and blue claps and empty rests with a moving playhead; the second row slides one beat left, a row of yellow and white dots shows what you hear, bars count the silent beats at every position.

slides.prompt: Move the second clapper ahead and find every position where no beat of the 12 is left silent. Press play to hear it.
slides.takeaway: 1, 6 and 11 beats ahead: 4 claps together, 8 alone, no silence. Every other position leaves 1 or 2 beats empty, and 12 beats ahead is unison again.

slides.heading: Claps that land together, by how far the second clapper is ahead
slides.note: Of the 8 claps in each 12-beat bar of Clapping Music, worked out from its pattern.

steps.label: Each step is clapped 8 or 12 times

slides.question: In Steve Reich’s Clapping Music, what does the second clapper do at each new step?
options: Moves the first beat to the end
slides.explanation: Each step shifts the same 12-beat pattern one beat ahead, so its first beat goes to the end. After 12 steps the two clappers are back in unison.
